stack: static SPA served via nginx / Docker

standards: structure: src/{components/{layout,sections,ui,common},hooks,lib,config,data,types}. Extract cross-cutting scroll/animation and accessibility concerns into src/hooks and src/lib; centralize third-party integration config (Web3Forms endpoint + access key via import.meta.env, WhatsApp number) in src/config; keep typed section content in src/data.
pattern: Custom hooks for scroll-driven animation (e.g. useScrollFrames, useSectionProgress) and useReducedMotion.
pattern: A single site-config module as the source of truth for external integrations.
pattern: Data-driven sections backed by typed models in src/data.
All third-party keys and endpoints are read from import.meta.env (Vite env) — never hard-coded string literals; ship .env.example with variable NAMES only.
Every scroll- or timer-driven animation honors prefers-reduced-motion via a single shared useReducedMotion hook.
No dead or placeholder links: every nav/footer anchor resolves to a real in-page section, or is removed.
Strict TypeScript; remove dead/unused modules (e.g. unused GlassCard) and unused env scaffolding.
Heavy canvas/particle/scroll-frame logic is extracted from section components into dedicated hooks/modules; section components stay presentational.
apply stack-standard security practices (see assessment findings)
preserve behaviour; no performance regressions vs the baseline

Introduce Vitest + React Testing Library (jsdom) with an `npm test` script wired into CI. Add characterization tests that pin CURRENT behaviour of the conversion-critical paths before refactoring: contact-form validation + submit success/error (with Web3Forms fetch mocked), navigation anchor resolution, and reduced-motion gating. These tests are the green-to-green safety net.
